description: Scaffold the ai-app-builder Node repo, wire plumby in through a single boundary module, define the closed enums, and stand up the hermetic test harness (scripted-provider agent builder + eval runner + fast-check config). Covers spec tasks 1.1, 2.1, 2.2 (Wave 0 partial + Wave 1 harness). Nothing else can be tested without this, so it comes first.
steps: Create /projects/sandbox/ai-app-builder/package.json: name "ai-app-builder", "type": "module", "engines": { "node": ">=20" }, "scripts": { "test": "node --test test/*.test.js", "eval": "node eval/run.js" }, dependency "plumby": "file:../plumby", devDependency "fast-check": "^4.9.0". Keep runtime deps minimal (Node stdlib + plumby only).

Run `cd /projects/sandbox/ai-app-builder && npm install` so node_modules links plumby (file:../plumby) and installs fast-check. Confirm `import { createAgent } from 'plumby/src/core/agent.js'` resolves (plumby's package.json "files" only lists bin/src/README, and it has no root export map, so import via the subpath 'plumby/src/...'; verify the resolved path works from a scratch node -e before writing the boundary).

Create src/engine/plumby.js as the SINGLE boundary re-export module. Re-export exactly these verified seams from the plumby package so the rest of the codebase never imports plumby directly: createAgent (from plumby src/core/agent.js), buildSystemPrompt (src/core/prompt.js), createScriptedProvider (src/providers/scripted.js), classifyCommand + REFUSE_RULES + CONFIRM_RULES (src/core/permissions.js), verifyTool (src/tools/verify.js), loadSkillTool (src/tools/load_skill.js), loadSkills (src/cli/project_context.js), indexSkills (src/core/skills.js), toViewEvent (src/web/events.js), computeDiff (src/web/diff.js), defaultTools + spawnSubagentTool + subagentTools (src/tools/index.js). Add a file-level comment stating this is the only place plumby may be imported. Do NOT reimplement any of these.

Create src/model/enums.js exporting the closed enums as frozen constant arrays/objects, matching the spec's data models exactly: Target_Category = ['web','full-stack-web','mobile','multi-target']; Target = ['web','backend','mobile','shared']; Project_Origin = ['blank','template','github-import','fork']; Connector_Category = ['database','auth','payments','hosting-deploy','storage','ai-model']; Memory_Mode = ['auto','manual','off']; and the classifier outcomes = ['allow','confirm','refuse']. Export small isValidX helper predicates. Freeze the arrays (Object.freeze).

Create test/support/scripted-agent.js exporting a helper (e.g. createScriptedAgent({ turns, cwd, tools, onEvent })) that builds a REAL plumby createAgent (imported via src/engine/plumby.js) wired to createScriptedProvider(turns). Use defaultTools + spawnSubagentTool, subagentProvider = the same scripted provider, subagentTools, buildSystemPrompt({ cwd }), a bounded maxIterations. No API key, no network. Mirror plumby eval/runner.js's createAgent assembly (read that file - it is the authoritative pattern).

Create eval/runner.js in this repo mirroring plumby/eval/runner.js: export runCase({ case, providerFor, maxIterations, onEvent }) and runSuite(...). Build the agent against an isolated fs.mkdtemp temp dir (os.tmpdir()), ALWAYS removed in a finally (even on throw). Use the safe bash policy (no confirm hook so confirm-class is denied by default). Hard iteration cap (default like plumby's DEFAULT_EVAL_MAX_ITERATIONS = 25). Run the objective check through plumby's exec (or node's child_process) NOT through the guard. Guard every phase so one case failure never aborts the suite. This is the shape the toolchain-backed property tests (7, 11, 13) will need later.

Create test/support/fc.js exporting the shared fast-check config: an fcConfig object with numRuns >= 100 (e.g. { numRuns: 100 }) to pass to fc.assert, and a tag helper propertyTag(n, title) returning the string `Feature: ai-app-builder, Property ${n}: ${title}`.

Add test/harness.test.js (node --test) proving the harness itself works: (a) a scripted-agent turn that calls a real tool (e.g. write_file then a text turn) runs through the real loop and produces the expected file / result with no network; (b) eval/runner.js runCase creates and then removes its temp dir (assert the dir does not exist after the run); (c) src/engine/plumby.js re-exports resolve (classifyCommand('rm -rf /') returns outcome 'refuse'); (d) enums are frozen and the isValid predicates work; (e) fc.js propertyTag produces the exact tag string and fcConfig.numRuns >= 100.
Create a minimal .gitignore (node_modules, and any temp/coverage artifacts) if one is needed.
acceptance_criteria: Running `cd /projects/sandbox/ai-app-builder && npm test` exits 0 with all test/*.test.js files passing (real pass counts reported).
src/engine/plumby.js is the only module that imports from the plumby package; a grep for the plumby import outside src/engine/plumby.js returns nothing.
src/model/enums.js exports the six closed enum sets exactly as specified and they are frozen.
eval/runner.js creates an fs.mkdtemp temp dir and removes it in a finally; the harness test asserts the dir is gone after a run.
test/support/scripted-agent.js builds a real plumby createAgent driven by the scripted provider with no key/network, and a test exercises a real tool call through it.
test/support/fc.js exports fcConfig with numRuns >= 100 and propertyTag producing 'Feature: ai-app-builder, Property N: {title}'.
verification: cd /projects/sandbox/ai-app-builder && npm test  (confirm all files pass, real counts, exit 0)
cd /projects/sandbox/ai-app-builder && grep -rn "from 'plumby" src test eval | grep -v 'src/engine/plumby.js'  (must return no matches)
findings: Scaffolded the ai-app-builder repo and stood up the hermetic harness. Files added: package.json (type module, engines node>=20, scripts test+eval, dep plumby file:../plumby, devDep fast-check ^4.9.0), .gitignore, src/engine/plumby.js (single boundary re-export module), src/model/enums.js, test/support/scripted-agent.js, test/support/fc.js, eval/runner.js, test/harness.test.js. `npm install` added 3 packages (plumby symlinked, fast-check installed). `npm test` is GREEN: 5 tests, 5 pass, 0 fail (test/harness.test.js). Grep check `grep -rn "from 'plumby" src test eval | grep -v src/engine/plumby.js` returns NO matches (both single- and double-quote forms), so src/engine/plumby.js is the sole plumby importer. NOTES for later features: (1) plumby's real package name is @2c2bhdhw9z-cell/plumby, but a `file:../plumby` dependency installs under the alias key `plumby`, so the bare subpath `import ... from 'plumby/src/...'` resolves correctly (verified via node -e before writing the boundary) — no relative fallback was needed. (2) plumby ships no root export map, so imports MUST use concrete source subpaths `plumby/src/...`. (3) The eval runner runs objective checks via node:child_process execFile('sh',['-c',cmd]) NOT through plumby's guard, matching plumby/eval/runner.js intent; plumby's exec seam was intentionally NOT added to the boundary since it is not one of the listed verified seams. (4) agent.send result shape: { text, stopReason, iterations, messages }; a text-only final scripted turn yields stopReason 'end_turn'. (5) Docker was not used (out of scope for this slice).
